subject: DPA negotiation: subprocessor & transfer terms for Dedicated vs Private deployments
messages:
From: Bethany Lowe <bethany.lowe@acme-solutions.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@acme-solutions.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA redlines for review (Acme / Redwood)

Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week — we had a productive session with our engineering and legal teams. Attached are Acme's initial redlines to Redwood's standard Data Processing Addendum. The primary items we want to resolve before procurement can move forward are:

- Subprocessor disclosure: we need a binding list or a guaranteed notice window and right to object for new subprocessors used in processing Acme data.
- Cross-border transfers: confirmation of the transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, or alternative safeguards) and an audited mapping of where customer data may be processed.
- Deployment modes: we need different commitments depending on whether this will be Dedicated (reserved infra) vs Private/VPC or on-premise deployments — specifically on data residency, key management, and subprocessors.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and recent penetration test summary.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept most of our edits and highlight any provisions likely to be a hard no so we can escalate. We'd like to close the DPA and execute via DocuSign by the end of next week if possible.

Attachments: DPA_Acme_Redlines_v1.docx

Regards,
Bethany Lowe
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Acme Solutions

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Lowe <bethany.lowe@acme-solutions.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines for review (Acme / Redwood)

Bethany — thanks for the thorough pass and the clear list. Looping in Neha (account lead) and Kimberly (legal) so we can align quickly.

Quick summary of where Redwood stands after an internal review:
- Subprocessors: we are open to a required notice period + objection right for material subprocessors. We typically provide a published subprocessor roster and 14 days' notice for additions; we can discuss extending to 30 days for material changes.
- Cross-border transfers: we rely on EU/UK SCCs where applicable and maintain appropriate safeguards for hosted customers. For Dedicated customers in a single region we can limit processing to that region to the extent technically possible.
- Deployment modes: Dedicated = reserved GPUs with tenant isolation; Private/VPC/on-prem = customer-managed environment options (we can support KMS/HSM integrations and limit Redwood-managed agents). We'll propose tailored language in the DPA to reflect these differences.
- Evidence: happy to provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II and pen-test summary under an NDA.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly will produce a Redwood redline that preserves the core protections Acme asks for while flagging operational constraints (I highlighted the subprocessor clause as an area where we may propose a notification-plus-objection model).
2) Quick technical sync (15–20m) to confirm what "region-limited processing" means for your infra team.
3) Exchange final redlines and execute via DocuSign.

I've attached a first-pass response (Redwood_DPA_response_v1.docx). Can we aim for a call tomorrow to go over the Dedicated vs Private distinctions?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_response_v1.docx

From: Bethany Lowe <bethany.lowe@acme-solutions.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@acme-solutions.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines for review (Acme / Redwood)

Alex, Neha, Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick reply and the response doc. Two clarifications from legal/infosec:

1) Notice window: Acme's legal team is comfortable with a notification approach but requires 30 days' notice for additions of any subprocessors that will have access to plaintext customer data or key material. 14 days is too short for our procurement/assessment workflows.

2) Cross-border transfers: we need explicit confirmation of the mechanism. For hosted instances we expect SCCs + Data Processing Annex; for Dedicated we want an explicit guarantee that data will not be transferred outside the selected region except for backups/maintenance with prior notice.

I've attached a short questionnaire our security team filled out — Samuel will coordinate a brief technical call to confirm the region/residency constraints.

Attachments: Acme_SSC_questions.pdf

Best,
Bethany

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Lowe <bethany.lowe@acme-solutions.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines for review (Acme / Redwood)

Bethany / Samuel — following up after consulting with our security and product teams. Below are concrete positions we can accept and proposed redline language for Section 4 (Subprocessors) and Section 7 (Cross-border transfers):

- Subprocessors (proposed position):
  * Hosted API: Redwood publishes a current subprocessor list; for any new subprocessor with access to customer plaintext or keys Redwood will provide 30 days' prior notice and allow Acme to raise objections. If Acme objects for legitimate security/compliance reasons, Redwood will engage in good-faith mitigations (alternative routing, contractual commitment, or temporary pause) while we attempt to address the issue.
  * Dedicated (reserved infra): Redwood limits subprocessors to those required for platform orchestration; no third-party processors will have access to customer application data stored in the tenant except with explicit written consent.
  * Private / VPC / On-premise: Redwood will not deploy external subprocessors inside customer-managed environments; any agent or operator script required for support will be under customer control or detailed in an appendix.

- Cross-border transfers: For Hosted customers Redwood relies on SCCs (or successor lawful mechanisms) plus technical controls; for Dedicated customers we commit to keeping processing within the contractually specified region except for narrow maintenance activities (which will be notified with reasonable advance notice). We will include this as a binding data transfer clause in the DPA.

- Evidence: we will provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and confirm availability of a penetration test summary under a CDA.

Kimberly's team will push a redline with the specific proposed text; if Acme confirms the 30-day notice for material subprocessors and accepts the Dedicated/Private delineation above, we'll prepare a final DPA for signature.

Can we set a 30-minute slot tomorrow for a short alignment call?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex / Kimberly / Neha —

Thanks — our teams are aligned on most items. We reviewed your proposed language and sent a tidy second redline with a few remaining asks:

- Please clarify retention and audit log custody: Acme cannot accept indefinite retention of audit logs containing PII past contract termination; propose a maximum of 7 years only when legally required.
- Confirm SOC 2 report delivery and redaction scope.
- Execution preference: Acme uses AdobeSign for most procurement and prefers that over DocuSign.

Attached: DPA_Acme_Redlines_v2.docx, SOC2_report_redacted.pdf

If you accept the small retention tweak and confirm AdobeSign is acceptable, we can circulate for signatures.

Best regards,
Bethany

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Lowe <bethany.lowe@acme-solutions.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final DPA confirmation & e-signature link (Acme / Redwood)

Bethany — great to get this across the finish line. Confirming Redwood accepts the revised language:

- Subprocessors: 30 days' notice for material subprocessors with the objection and mitigation path described. For Dedicated deployments, we will ensure that orchestration-only subprocessors cannot access tenant application data; for Private/VPC/on-prem we will adopt a no-external-subprocessor model unless explicitly agreed.
- Cross-border transfers: SCCs (or future equivalent) for Hosted; contractual region-lock for Dedicated with maintenance exceptions (notifications + limited scope).
- Retention: Redwood agrees to cap audit log retention to 7 years unless a longer period is required by law; we will provide a phrased exception for lawful hold scenarios.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II (redacted) delivered; pen-test summary available under CDA.

We are happy to execute in AdobeSign per your preference — I've prepared the final DPA (attached) and started an AdobeSign envelope. Link below to review and sign: https://app.adobesign.com/review/ENVELOPE-98765-RDW

Next steps:
1) Acme to review the attached final DPA and confirm signers.
2) Neha will follow up on commercial terms (pricing/seat commitments) in a separate thread.
3) Once signed, Kimberly will coordinate SOC2 delivery and a short security onboarding call.

Thanks again — excited to get Acme onboarded.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_Final_for_Signature.pdf
